requirements.title: ASYNCHRONOUS= value is YES or NO
requirements.definition: The ASYNCHRONOUS= scalar default character expression shall evaluate to YES or NO.

requirements.title: Omitted ASYNCHRONOUS= defaults to NO
requirements.definition: If ASYNCHRONOUS= is omitted, the default value is NO.

pending.asynchronous-default-no: Concrete INQUIRE plan: OPEN a named file on a known unit omitting ASYNCHRONOUS=, prefill a default-character ASYNCHRONOUS inquiry variable with a nonmatching sentinel such as '#########', then INQUIRE by unit with ASYNCHRONOUS=. Per 12.10.2.5, ASYNCHRONOUS= is assigned NO when the connection does not allow asynchronous input/output; assert exactly the token NO (with only blank padding if the variable is longer). A supplemental negative source-control may attempt asynchronous I/O on the default connection, but no diagnostic is required by this prose default rule.

review_rationale: Source registration for the OPEN statement and its specifiers, 12.5.6.1-12.5.6.19 (batch151). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across four rounds. Round 1 found required OPEN defaults with only generic plans and required default tokens over-suppressed as unobservable; both are now concrete sentinel-prefilled INQUIRE plans (ACCESS, ASYNCHRONOUS, BLANK, DECIMAL, DELIM, FORM, PAD, LEADING_ZERO, SIGN, and ROUND as set membership). Rounds 2 and 3 found that INQUIRE(POSITION=) reports connection STATE, not the omitted OPEN token, and that a re-OPEN plan observes 12.5.6.1 p6 rather than the POSITION default; the omitted POSITION= token is now recorded as not portably observable, as are the STATUS and ENCODING default tokens. The eight numbered rules R1204-R1207 and C1203-C1206 were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
